An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf retr 5.1
div.ab: Quodsi fugiendo domum sacerdotis uel curiam eius intrauerit, eandem securitatem et pacem habeat quam et apud ecclesiam, dum tamen sacerdotis domus et curia in fundo ecclesie consistant.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 630 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

div.ab: But if in fleeing he enters the priest's house or his courtyard, let him have the same security and peace as at the church, provided that the priest's house and courtyard stand on the Church's land.
